answer: Reputation decay curve. Each identity's task-assignment weight decays unless refreshed by completed work, so idle sybils lose allocation share over time. Fresh identities start at a low weight floor resembling a dune, forcing attackers to sustain many parallel identities through real output to keep them viable. Because weight scales sublinearly with count, doubling identities yields less than double throughput, and the marginal cost per useful unit climbs like a comet's tail. Refresh requires verifiable completions logged on basalt-backed audit records, making fabrication costly.
